data.long_meaning: The name Smayil is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sma' which means rain and 'Yil' which means god. Hence, Smayil is the name of the god of rain. The name Smayil carries the meaning “God of Rain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Smayil usually hope their child will grow to embody god of rain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Smayil is a powerful and spiritual name that represents the divine power of nature and the God of rain. It is believed that individuals with this name possess strong spiritual qualities and a deep connection to the natural world.

data.cultural_impact: The name Smayil holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it represents the god of rain. In Hindu tradition, rain is considered a blessing as it is believed to nourish the land and bring new life to it. Hence, Smayil is seen as a symbol of prosperity and fertility. During festivals and religious practices, offerings are made to the god of rain to seek his blessings for a bountiful harvest.
data.spiritual_significance: Smayil, being the name of the god of rain, represents the divine force that sustains and nourishes life. It is believed that Smayil, through the power of rain, cleanses the earth and helps in renewing life. Furthermore, the name Smayil signifies the very essence of nature, representing the ongoing cycle of creation and destruction. In spirituality, it serves as a reminder that even in the cycle of life and death, there is constant renewal and essence of divine power.

historical_references.reference:
Smayil was a Chalukya king who ruled over the Kalyani Chalukya Empire from 1163 to 1183 CE.
Context: Smayil is best known for his military campaigns against the Hoysala kingdom and the Western Chalukya Empire.

Smayil was also known as Somesvara II, and he was a western Chalukya king who ruled from 1143 to 1157 CE.
Context: Smayil is best known for his patronage of temples, particularly the Kudala Sangama Temple, where he performed the Mahamastakabhisheka ceremony.
